Subject: Post-demo: buyer map + deployment tradeoffs (latency vs cost)

Thanks again for your time earlier today — really appreciate the open conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Highlights from the demo and what I heard as the core decision levers: 
- Latency SLO: target p95 around 100–120ms for typical inference (512 tokens).
- Cost sensitivity: want to understand unit economics across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (we discussed net per-inference cost and 1M-token equivalents).
- Data residency / PHI: Acme will need clarity on private/deid options and KMS controls.
- Decision stakeholders: product/econ buyer (Lydia), procurement (Mark/Procurement team), InfoSec (Clara) — we need to map procurement timeline and required evidence.

Deliverables I will action this week:
1) Share a lightweight cost/latency model that compares Hosted, Dedicated (reserved pools), and Private deployment for your workload — spreadsheet attached (acme-latency-cost-modeling.xlsx).
2) Post-demo notes and recording excerpt (post-demo-notes.pdf).
3) Draft mutual action plan (short) to align procurement steps and timeline.

Ask from your side: please confirm the economic buyer and procurement contact (Mark?) and whether InfoSec requires a full SOC2 package + runbook or a targeted evidence pack. Also let me know availability for a 30-min follow-up next week to run through the pricing delta and procurement path.

Proposed next step: 30 min on Tue or Wed to walk the cost model and confirm procurement requirements.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Vanessa — great recap.

Couple of clarifications from our side:
- Economic buyer: Mark Reyes (CFO) will own spend approval for any Reserved/Dedicated commitment; I will be the product sponsor. Mark is cc'd here.
- Procurement lead: Dan O'Malley will run the SOW/contract steps — Dan, look for a follow-up from Vanessa.
- InfoSec: Clara will be the technical reviewer; she needs to know exactly what evidence is available for PHI (SOC2 Type II, KMS/HSM integration details, data retention + deletion procedures).

On decision criteria specifics:
- Latency: we are targeting p95 < 120ms for single-request inference with typical 512-token inputs; tail latency is important for UX.
- Cost: our internal target is to keep inference spend predictable — roughly equivalent to <= $X per 1M tokens (we'll convert once we see your model).
- Deployment: preferred is Dedicated in our cloud region (us-west) if the price delta vs Hosted is reasonable; Private on-prem is a last resort due to ops overhead.

Can you provide:
1) a clear comparison table (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with expected p95 for 256/512 tokens and estimated monthly unit cost for our volume (we're forecasting ~10M tokens/mo in Q4).
2) SOC2 artifacts or a link to your security package and a short note on KMS/HSM support and data residency controls.

I've attached a short list of procurement/security questions we usually use (acme-internal-questions.docx).

I'm available Tue 10:00–12:00 PT or Wed 09:00–11:00 PT next week — either works.

Best,
Lydia Park
VP Product, Acme Health
lpark@acmehealth.com

Great — thanks for the clear owner list, Lydia. Quick confirmations and what we'll bring to the follow-up: 

1) Pricing summary: RDW-12984-pricing-summary.pdf attached. This includes a compact table comparing expected p95 latency (256/512 tokens) and monthly cost buckets for Hosted, Dedicated (reserved), and Private. Highlights: Dedicated gives predictable per-token economics with lower unit cost at commit levels; Hosted is fastest to go-live with no initial commitment; Private gives the strictest controls at higher ops cost.

2) Security artifacts: Ben will attach a SOC2 evidence pack and a short KMS integration note before the call. For PHI we recommend Dedicated with Customer-managed KMS in the cloud region you choose; we can run a compliance scoping call with Clara if helpful.

3) SLA / SLOs: proposed baseline SLA 99.9% uptime for Dedicated/Hosted with latency SLOs we can tier across small/medium/heavy workloads — we'll surface options in the pricing PDF. We also support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant to preserve availability during capacity constraints.

4) Next call: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 10:00 PT (30 minutes) — does that still work for everyone? I'll send a calendar invite once we have confirmation.

Action items assigned:
- Vanessa/Ben: deliver final pricing + SOC2 summary (Fri EOD).
- Dan: confirm procurement contract timeline and any mandatory clauses for Acme.
- Clara: if you'd like a runbook or evidence checklist ahead of the technical call, share the preferred format.

Thanks — looking forward to the follow-up.
